title: Add OTel collector config examples for quickstart templates (local dev + production) with redaction
author: Sergio Costa
release_notes: Add copy/paste-able OpenTelemetry Collector configs for quickstart templates, including local docker-compose defaults and a production-oriented example with attribute allowlisting and redaction.
body: Context: As part of the Quickstart Templates rollout, we want a default local-dev observability path that (a) works out of the box, (b) matches Redwood tracing conventions, and (c) does not accidentally leak secrets/PII via spans/logs/attributes. This PR adds two concrete OpenTelemetry Collector configuration examples that template repos can reference and that we can point users to from docs/troubleshooting. What’s in this PR: 1) New collector configs: - collector/config.local-dev.yaml: default OTLP receiver (grpc/http), batch + memory limiter, resource attribution, and a conservative redaction/allowlist policy appropriate for developer laptops. - collector/config.production.example.yaml: production-oriented example (still generic) showing how to wire redaction + attribute allowlisting and keep cardinality under control. 2) New docker-compose example: - docker-compose.otel.local.yaml to run otelcol-contrib with the local-dev config and expose 4317/4318. 3) README updates: - docs snippet describing how template apps should point OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT at the local collector; notes on when to prefer http vs grpc; and guidance on verifying traces are flowing. Redaction / safety details: - We explicitly drop or redact sensitive attributes commonly observed in HTTP/gateway environments (Authorization, Cookie, Set-Cookie, X-Api-Key, and template telemetry tags when misconfigured). - We include an allowlist pattern for redwood.* attributes and select http.* attributes; everything else remains opt-in (to avoid high-cardinality surprises). - We document how to extend the allowlist safely for custom app attributes. Example snippet (local-dev): processors: attributes/redaction: actions: - key: http.request.header.authorization action: delete - key: http.request.header.cookie action: delete - key: http.request.header.x-api-key action: delete - key: redwood.api_key action: delete - key: enduser.id action: delete (templates shouldn’t set this; defensive) transform/sanitize: trace_statements: - context: span statements: - replace_pattern(attributes["http.target"], "\\?.*", "") Notes: - We intentionally do not add any exporter credentials guidance beyond standard env vars; users should use their platform’s secret manager. - The production example includes comments on enabling a filelog receiver only when needed and how to avoid logging request/response bodies. Testing: - Adds a small CI validation step that runs otelcol-contrib config validation against both configs (caught a typo in an earlier revision). - Local smoke: ran docker-compose.otel.local.yaml and verified traces from the Python template show up in Grafana Tempo with expected resource attributes and without header leakage. Follow-ups (not blocking): - Align exact attribute allowlist with the final docs page under redwood-docs/pr-844 once that lands; we may want to keep one canonical source of truth. - Consider adding an optional ‘debug exporter’ block for local troubleshooting, but default should stay safe (no payload dumps).
commits: add local-dev otel collector config with safe processors
add production example collector config with allowlist + redaction
add docker-compose for local collector + docs notes
ci: validate otelcol configs in workflow
review_conversation: Allison Grant: Can we be explicit that headers should not be captured by default? Even with redaction, it’s easy to miss a key. Also, please avoid encouraging high-cardinality attributes in examples (e.g., full URLs with query strings).

Sergio Costa (author): Updated both configs to (1) delete common header keys defensively, (2) strip query strings from http.target, and (3) add comments that header capture should remain off unless explicitly needed for debugging.
Christine Wong: For production example, can we add guidance about memory_limiter + batch sizing? We’ve seen template apps overwhelm collectors in dev clusters when batching is too aggressive.

Sergio Costa (author): Added recommended defaults and comments (memory_limiter check_interval, limit_mib, spike_limit_mib) and kept batch settings conservative. Also clarified that production example is a starting point and should be load-tested.
Monica Patel: Templates need a dead-simple local path. Are we okay with both 4317 and 4318 exposed and documenting the one we prefer?

Sergio Costa (author): Yes—local config exposes both; docs recommend HTTP (4318) for easier proxy compatibility, but note gRPC is fine if users prefer it. This matches the template default env var blocks we’ve been using.
Caleb Johnson: Minor: processors order—redaction should run before batching; also, can we avoid adding any user identifiers (enduser.id) to examples to prevent people copy/pasting?
Sergio Costa (author): Re-ordered processors; removed any mention of setting enduser.id and kept a defensive delete rule only (commented).
Allison Grant: Looks good now. Approving once CI is green.
CI: validate otelcol configs failed (unknown processor name) on config.production.example.yaml.
Sergio Costa (author): Fixed processor name + reran; CI now green.
